content.text: No renewal or auto-renewal mechanic exists anywhere; the term is evergreen and exit is easy.

input.quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
input.rationale: This is a task-by-task consultancy with an evergreen term rather than a fixed term with renewals: § 2 runs from signature "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6", and § 6(a) lets either party (including us) exit "for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice" whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding. There is no "automatically renew" mechanic, no renewal term length, and no non-renewal notice window anywhere in the document (searches for renewal, term extension and rate-increase-on-renewal language return nothing), so every element of both the preferred and fallback positions is conditional on automatic renewal and is not triggered — the rule is effectively not applicable, and the bargain is better than the fallback because we can exit on 15 days' notice with no window to miss. Noted but not flagged here: § 3(b) allows Contractor to "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" with no cap, but that is a mid-term pricing right rather than a renewal uplift, so it belongs to the pricing rule and is not double-flagged under RENEWAL.
